Recreating one of my Nonna’s most loved recipes this Mother’s Day… insalata di polpo e patate 🤍 (Octopus & Potato Salad)

A simple, nostalgic dish that takes me right back to walking the aisles with her. Made with fresh, everyday ingredients @foodbasicson Proof that simple, good ingredients, and a little love, is all you need to make something meaningful – just like Nonna taught me.

Recipe:
Ingredients 
2 kg Octopus
6-8 medium Yellow/yukon gold potatoes
1/2 cup Fresh parsley
Juice of 1 lemon
1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil
Salt to taste 

Preparation
1. Cook the octopus in boiling water until tender, then let it cool completely.
2. Boil the potatoes until fork tender and allow them to cool.
3. Prepare the dressing by combining olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, and salt.
4. Peel the potatoes, then cut the cooled octopus and potatoes into even cubes.
5. Add everything to a bowl, pour over the dressing, and mix gently to combine.

Serving suggestion
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

caption:
Friselle are a traditional twice-baked bread from Southern Italy, especially popular in Puglia during the summer months. The bread is baked until completely dry and crisp, then lightly soaked with water so it softens just enough while still keeping its signature crunch. We get ours from a local bakery, and it becomes the perfect base for olive oil, juicy tomatoes, and all the flavours layered on top.

It’s simple pantry cooking at its best and comes together in minutes after a day at the beach. Growing up, this was always an effortless summer lunch that somehow tasted even better eaten outside in the heat. This is every nonna’s version of a “girl dinner.”

Friselle con Tonno
Total Time: 15 minutes
Servings: 4–6

Ingredients:

6 friselle
3 cans Italian tuna in olive oil
1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved
1 medium red onion, thinly sliced
2 tbsp capers
Oregano, to taste
Salt, to taste
Olive oil, generous drizzle
Basil for topping

Instructions:

Prepare the Topping:
In a large bowl, combine cherry tomatoes, tuna, red onion, capers, oregano, salt, and a generous drizzle of olive oil. Mix gently until combined.

Soften the Friselle:
Quickly dip each frisella into water for just a few seconds. They should soften slightly while still staying crunchy in the centre.

Assemble:
Arrange the softened friselle on a serving platter and spoon the tomato and tuna mixture generously over top.

Serve:
Finish with extra olive oil and basil. Enjoy immediately with a glass of wine, al fresco 😉

#friselle #pugliafood #frisellepugliesi #nonna #nonnamaxxing

Nonna Flo and I’s favourite sandwich: Mortadella, stracciatella, and our favourite @_favuzzi pistachio pesto. 

This is a must-try combo, and the pistachio pesto takes it to another level! Of course we had to pair it with an ice cold, refreshing @_favuzzi Sicilian soda. Buon appetito!

Prep time: 5 minutes | Serves 2–4

Ingredients
1 homemade or store-bought focaccia, or bread of choice
2–3 tbsp Favuzzi Pistachio Pesto
150–200 g mortadella
125 g stracciatella cheese

Preparation
1. Slice the focaccia in half horizontally.

2. Spread the pistachio pesto evenly over the bottom half of the focaccia.

3. Gently layer the mortadella over the pesto without folding it to keep it light and airy.

4. Add the stracciatella cheese evenly on top of the mortadella.

5. Close the sandwich with the top half of the focaccia.

6. Slice into portions and serve immediately.

Cotolette di melanzane stuffed with smoked scamorza and speck 🧀🍆

5 small Italian eggplants
1 ball of scamorza or mozzarella
100g speck or prosciutto
About 2 cups breadcrumbs, more or less 
3 eggs
Salt to taste

Preheat the oven to 485°F. Slice the eggplant lengthwise into pieces about 1/4 inch thick. Dip each slice into the egg, then coat evenly in breadcrumbs. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking tray and drizzle generously with olive oil. Bake for 15–20 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden and crisp.

Meanwhile, place the speck or prosciutto on a parchment-lined tray and bake for 5–10 minutes until crispy. Keep an eye on it because it can burn quickly.

Pair the eggplant slices together with a piece of scamorza and some crispy speck or prosciutto in the middle. Sandwich them together and return to the oven for another 5 minutes, just until the cheese melts.

Enjoy hot, warm, or straight from the fridge the next day because they’re so good cold too.

caption:
RECIPE: ⬇️Calzone di cipolla 🧅 Onion, olives, and tomatoes in a flaky white wine based dough 🍕 

This is one of my favourite Pugliese traditions ever!! We eat this all year round but especially this month for San Giuseppe ❤️ if you make this (or if you make it differently) let me know 🥰🥰 

Makes 1 large pizza tray, 2 small trays, or 3 round pans (about 10”)

Use a scale to weigh each ingredient in grams for accuracy (Nonna Flo doesn’t measure, but I weighed everything so that you can try it too 🥰)

Dough
1 kg flour
500 g white wine, slightly warmed (not boiling)
200 g olive oil
20 g salt

Filling
3 lbs yellow, white, or spring onions (sponsali)
3 peeled San Marzano tomatoes from the can crushed with your hands OR 2 Roma tomatoes Black olives — Peranzana, Baresana, or Kalamata (what we use) 
60 ml milk
1 tbsp ricotta forte or a handful of pecorino
Salt to taste

Dough
Make a well in the flour. Add the white wine and olive oil and start incorporating with your hands. Once it comes together, add the salt and knead until smooth and elastic. Let rest 1 hour covered with plastic wrap. 

Filling
Chop the onions and cook in a pot over medium heat with the milk and salt. Stir until they start to sweat (about 5 minutes). Add the pelati and olives and cook until the onions are soft (about 10 minutes). Let cool slightly.

Preheat oven to 425°F. Grease trays with lard.
Divide the dough in half (one piece slightly larger for the base). Roll thin, slightly larger than the tray. Spread the onion filling evenly. Roll the second piece thin and place on top. Fold the bottom layer over to seal.
Brush with olive oil, make a few small openings on top, and bake on the middle rack 35–45 minutes, until deeply golden.

caption:
It’s not summer in our house without Acquacale (cialledda). A traditional dish from Puglia that immediately brings us back to our roots.

It’s a classic dish served cold on hot summer days, often during or after a day by the sea. 

It is a mix of crunchy bread, ripe tomatoes, fresh vegetables, and good olive oil coming together in the most effortless way.

We finish it with @_favuzzi Coratina olive oil, made with the Coratina olive, the queen of Puglia 👑 It ties everything together beautifully. Buon appetito!

Recipe:
Prep time: 10 minutes | Serves 4–6
Ingredients
Garlic crispy focaccia @_favuzzi 
1 pint cherry tomatoes
1 small red onion, thinly sliced
1 cucumber, peeled, sliced lengthwise, then cut into half moons
2 celery stalks with leaves, chopped
2 tbsp capers
Fresh basil
Salt to taste
@_favuzzi Coratina olive oil

Preparation
Soak the sliced red onion in cold water with a pinch of salt for about 10 minutes to mellow out the sharpness. Drain well before using.

Tear the focaccia into bite-sized pieces and place in a large bowl.
Slice the cherry tomatoes in half and add to the bowl.

Add the drained red onion.

Add the cucumber, chopped celery (including the leaves) and capers.
Tear in plenty of fresh basil and season with salt.

Drizzle generously with olive oil and toss everything together.
Let sit for a few minutes so the bread absorbs the flavours, then serve.

Serving suggestion
Best enjoyed slightly softened, once the bread has soaked up the juices and olive oil.

caption:
Zeppole di San Giuseppe (Gluten-Free / Senza Glutine) 
RECIPE ⬇️

Crema Pasticcera (enough for 12 zeppole) 
800ml milk, 8 egg yolks, 110g corn starch, 200g sugar, lemon peel (or half a lemon pierced with a fork - love this trick from @lafocacciaqueen 🍋💛).

Heat the milk with lemon peel until warm. In a bowl, whisk the sugar and yolks until smooth, then add the corn starch and mix until fully combined and fluffy. Slowly add the warm milk to the egg mixture, then return everything to the pot. Heat over medium-low, stirring continuously, until thickened. About 3 minutes. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface, and refrigerate until cool before using.

Pasta Choux (makes 12 zeppole) 
400g water, 120g unsalted butter, 250g Caputo gluten-free flour, around 440g whole eggs (for me this was about 9 small eggs).

Start with water, butter, flour, and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-low heat, mixing continuously until it comes together. Add eggs one at a time, making sure each is fully incorporated before adding the next. Pipe onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake at 375. Once done, turn the oven off, crack the door open, and let them cool in the oven to prevent collapsing.

Fill with your favourite crema, dust with powdered sugar, and enjoy!

#KnorrPartner These Italian-inspired Peri-Peri Chicken & Vegetable Skewers bring together the bold heat of peri-peri chicken and the bright, herby flavours of a traditional salmoriglio. 

Knorr® Roasted Chicken Premium Flavour Base forms the foundation of a sweet and spicy marinade that keeps the chicken juicy and flavourful on the grill. Finished with a fresh peri-peri salmoriglio, this recipe is perfect for summer entertaining! 

For the Chicken Skewers
2 Tbsp. (30 mL) honey
2 Tbsp. (30 mL) olive oil
1 Tbsp. (15 mL) @Knorrca Chicken Flavour Base
1 Tbsp. (15 mL) Peri-Peri sauce
1 tsp. (5 mL) smoked paprika
2 garlic cloves, minced
¼ tsp. (1.25 mL) freshly ground black pepper
1 lb (450 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
1 red bell pepper, cut into chunks
1 red onion, cut into wedges
Wooden or metal skewers

For the Peri-Peri Salmoriglio
¼ cup (60 mL) olive oil
2 Tbsp. (30 mL) fresh lemon juice
1 garlic clove, finely grated
2 Tbsp. finely chopped fresh parsley
½ tsp. dried oregano
1 bird’s eye chili, finely chopped
1 Tbsp. Peri-Peri sauce
1 tsp. red wine vinegar
Pinch of salt to taste

Directions
In a medium bowl, whisk together honey, olive oil, Knorr® Chicken Flavour Base, peri-peri sauce, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper until smooth.
Add the chicken thighs and toss until evenly coated. Let marinate while you prepare the vegetables, or refrigerate for up to 2 hours for deeper flavour.
Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high heat and lightly oil the grates. Thread the chicken, red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, and red onion alternately onto skewers.
Grill the skewers, turning occasionally, for 10–12 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through and lightly charred.
While the skewers cook, prepare the peri-peri salmoriglio. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, parsley, oregano, bird’s eye chili, smoked paprika, peri-peri sauce, vinegar, and salt. Stir until combined.
Transfer the skewers to a serving platter and generously spoon the peri-peri salmoriglio over top before serving #KnorrPartner @knorrca

caption:
Sbriciolata with Ricotta & Black Cherry Jam 🤍

This is a quick and easy version of a sbriciolata (with melted butter instead of cold butter that you’d have to work into the flour) I’ve made this 5 times in 2 weeks for Easter and other events and it is so good! 

I highly, highly recommended using lievito vanigliato (Italian vanilla baking powder). I have never had trouble finding it. No frills, metro, fortinos, longos, Walmart etc. It adds the most amazing vanilla flavour. Trust me, you’ll be using this for all your desserts!! 😍😍
 
Ingredients:
350g 00 flour
120g salted butter, melted
2 eggs
60g granulated sugar
1/2 pack (8g) lievito vanigliato OR 8g baking powder + a splash of vanilla
1 container ricotta (475g)
40–60g powdered sugar (adjust to taste)
Jam of choice 

Instructions:
Whisk melted butter, eggs, and sugar until light and airy.
Add flour and lievito vanigliato and mix until a smooth dough forms. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix ricotta with powdered sugar until smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust sweetness as needed.
Grease a fluted tart pan with a removable bottom.
Press half the dough into the base, then add a layer of black cherry jam followed by the ricotta filling.
Take the remaining dough and crumble it over the top with your hands.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for about 35–40 minutes, or until golden.
Let it cool completely, then finish with a dusting of powdered sugar.

Store in the fridge for 4 days covered with plastic wrap.

caption:
BOCCONOTTI “little bites” are a classic Italian pastry found in many regions of Italy. Every region, every town, and every household makes them a little different - thats the beauty of a family recipe! We are from the Puglia region 🥰 

The dough is rich because of the strutto, which gives it a tender almost shortbread like texture. The process itself is simple and straightforward. So rewarding and loved by so many 🥰❤️ 

If you grew up with these/make them, let me know your favourite filling and I will give it a try! 😊 

Ingredients
 - 500g flour
 - 225g strutto (lard) or butter
 - 2 whole eggs
 - 2 egg yolks
 - 150g sugar
 - Zest of 1 lemon
 - 2 tsp lievito vanigliato OR 2 tsp baking powder + a splash of vanilla extract
 - Jam of choice
 - 1 egg for egg wash

Whisk together the eggs, egg yolks, sugar, and lemon zest until light and slightly airy.
Add the flour and mix until the texture becomes sandy.
Add the strutto and work it in with your hands until a smooth dough forms.
Cover and let rest for 10 minutes. Preheat oven to 350°F.
Place your bocconotti molds on a baking tray.
Roll small pieces of dough into balls, flatten into disks, and press into the molds. Trim any excess.
Fill with jam.
Top with another disk of dough, press and seal the edges well so they stay closed while baking, and trim again.
Brush with egg wash.
Bake until golden. About 20 minutes. 
Let cool slightly before removing from the molds. Dust with powdered sugar.

Nonna Flo and I’s go-to summer pasta: orecchiette alla crudaiola. It is fresh, simple, and full of flavour, and it’s truly not summer without this! It is loaded with juicy tomatoes, lots of basil, and @_favuzzi sun dried tomato pesto.

Since this dish is so fresh, we chose the @_favuzzi finishing oil made with the Coratina olive, the queen of Puglia. An iconic variety from the birthplace of Italian olive oil, and the Favuzzi family’s region of origin (something we have in common).

The Coratina is celebrated for its vibrant character and exceptional richness, with a pronounced flavour. A final drizzle truly takes this dish to another level.

Finished with a grating of ricotta salata, something you simply can’t do without, and ready in the time it takes to cook the pasta. Buon appetito!

Recipe:
Prep time: 10 minutes | Cook time: 18 minutes | Serves 5–6

Ingredients
1 pack @_favuzzi orecchiette
2 pints cherry tomatoes
1–2 cloves garlic, smashed or cut into large pieces (to be removed before serving)
Fresh basil, hand-torn
1/4 cup Favuzzi sun dried tomato pesto
Drizzle of Favuzzi Coratina olive oil
Ricotta salata or pecorino romano, grated
Salt to taste

Preparation
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the orecchiette according to package
directions. Stir often.
Meanwhile, slice the cherry tomatoes in half and add them to a large bowl. Season with salt.
Add the smashed garlic, plenty of hand-torn basil, and a drizzle of olive oil. Let it sit while the
pasta cooks.
Once the pasta is al dente, drain and add it directly to the bowl with the tomatoes while still hot.
Add the sun dried tomato pesto and toss everything together until well combined.
Remove the garlic pieces.
Finish with freshly grated ricotta salata or pecorino romano.

Serving suggestion:
Serve immediately, at room temperature, or cold with an extra drizzle of olive oil.

caption:
EPISODE 1 of my ONE-DOUGH series 🍞🥖🥪🫓 
If dough feels intimidating, this series is for you. You don’t need dozens of recipes or fancy techniques to make bread you’ll be proud to serve. It all starts with one simple dough:

(90% hydration) 
Ingredients:

500g bread flour

450g lukewarm water

15g fine sea salt

8g instant yeast

How to make it:

Add flour and salt into a big bowl and mix it really well.

Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm water, then pour it in and mix vigorously with hands or a wooden spoon until it comes together (sticky is perfect! don’t add more flour!).

Cover and let it rest for 30 minutes.

Wet or oil your hands, grab the dough, lift it, and fold it over itself a few times to create tension. Cover and let it rest again.

Repeat this “fold and rest” two more times. (3 RESTS TOTAL - 30 min each). This gentle technique builds the dough’s strength, helps it rise, and gives it a light, airy crumb.

After the 3rd rest - it is ready to use for all the recipes to come. 

That’s all! 🥰

caption:
@conestoga_eggs challenged me with The Stories We Cook, because every dish carries a memory 💛 Proudly local, proudly a part of your story! 
 
I invited my Nonna to share one of her most special recipes, Rigatoni al Forno. A Sunday classic that has been at the heart of our family table for generations. I still remember rolling the tiny meatballs with my little hands beside her, trying to make them just like hers.
 
This recipe deserves only the best ingredients, and that’s why we used Conestoga Farms’ eggs, known for their naturally golden yolks that come from hens fed a diet with marigold extract, a natural source of lutein.
 
There’s no feeling quite like the comfort of a Sunday in Nonna’s kitchen. I hope you feel a bit of it in yours too ♥️
 
Ingredients:
6 @conestoga_eggs 
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1 small white onion, finely chopped
1 clove of garlic, peeled
2 jars of passata (tomato puree)
1 lb ground beef or veal (or mixed) 
¼ cup parsley, finely chopped.
¼ cup breadcrumbs
¼ cup grated parmigiano reggiano
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 pack (500 g) pasta such as rigatoni
2 packs of mozzarella, 340g balls
Salt and pepper, to taste
 
Directions:
Finely chop a carrot, celery stalk, and white onion. Sauté in extra virgin olive oil with a peeled garlic clove until soft. Add tomato purée, season with salt, lower the heat and let simmer gently.
 
In a large bowl, mix ground beef with an egg, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Form small meatballs and drop them directly into the simmering tomato sauce. Cook gently, covered, until tender and fully cooked.
 
Boil 5 eggs until hard, cool under cold water, peel, and slice. Dice the mozzarella.
 
Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain, add ladles of sauce and mix thoroughly.
 
In a large baking dish, layer pasta, mozzarella, egg slices, and Parmigiano. Repeat the layers, finishing with cheese and more hard boiled eggs.
 
Bake at 400°F until bubbly and crispy.

Occhi di Santa Lucia RICETTA / RECIPE below 
These glazed taralli, Occhi di Santa Lucia, are a traditional treat from Puglia, made starting December 13 for Saint Lucy’s Day and during the holiday season. With just a few simple ingredients, the taralli have a very neutral, sweet flavor that comes alive once dipped in a sugar and lemon glaze, which my Nonna calls “Gilepp.”

Ingredienti/Ingredients
500 g farina 00 | 00 flour 
160 g vino bianco | white wine
120 g olio extravergine di oliva | extra virgin olive oil
Pizzico di sale | Pinch of salt

Glassa/Glaze
Zucchero a velo | Powdered sugar
Succo di 1/2 limone | Juice of 1/2 lemon (optional) 
q.b Latte o acqua | Milk or water, added gradually to reach desired consistency

PROCEDIMENTO / DIRECTIONS ⬇️

Mescola farina, olio e vino poco alla volta.
Aggiungi il sale e impasta fino a ottenere un impasto liscio.
Lascia riposare 20 minuti.
Preriscalda il forno a 200°C.
Forma i taralli e cuoci per 20 minuti.
Glassali e lascia asciugare per tutta la notte.

⬇️
Make a well with the flour on a work surface. Add the olive oil, then incorporate the white wine slowly. Add a pinch of salt and knead until a smooth dough forms. Let rest for 20 minutes.

caption:
STUFFED ARTICHOKES IN TOMATO SAUCE 😍 Carciofi ripieni al sugo… 
The dish of my childhood. If you’ve never had stuffed artichokes simmered in tomato sauce, this is your sign. Fibre and protein!!

Here’s the full recipe ⬇️
INGREDIENTS
 • 10 medium artichokes
 • 1 lb ground beef, veal, or a mix
 • 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
 • 1/2 cup chopped parsley
 • 2 eggs
 • 1/4 cup pecorino or parm
 • 2–3 garlic cloves
 • 1 large bottle passata (about 700ml)
 • Fresh basil
 • Olive oil
 • Salt to taste
 • 1 lemon

HOW TO CLEAN THE ARTICHOKES
To prevent browning, fill a large bowl with cold water and squeeze in the juice of 1-2 lemons. Drop the lemon halves in too. (Rub some lemon on your hands. It helps prevent staining.)

Peel off the tough outer leaves until you reach the lighter, more tender ones (the heart).

Cut off the pointy top.

Open up the leaves (with thumbs or smack it gently on a surface) and scoop out the hairy centre with a spoon.

Trim and peel the stem, removing the tough outer layer but keeping the tender core.

Place cleaned artichokes straight into the lemon water to prevent browning.

DIRECTIONS 
In a bowl, mix ground meat, breadcrumbs, parsley, eggs, pecorino (or parm), and a good pinch of salt.
Pack the meat nice and compact in between the leaves of each artichoke.

In a large pot, heat olive oil and sauté crushed garlic until fragrant. Don’t burn the garlic. 
Place the artichokes face down to brown the meat slightly.
Pour in passata and enough water so the artichokes are submerged). Add fresh basil and salt to taste. 
Cover and simmer on medium-low for at least 1 hour, until the stems are fork tender. 
Serve with pasta or eat them on their own.
And don’t forget the crunchy bread for the scarpetta at the end 🇮🇹

MAFALDE AI FUNGHI RECIPE🍄❤️
Serves 4-6 
Ingredients:
- 500 g mafaldine pasta
- 6 cups mixed mushrooms (I used oyster, cremini, porcini, and portobello)
- 1 medium onion
- 1 cup white wine
- 2 cups heavy cream
- 2 tbsp truffle paste
- Olive oil
- Salt
- Parmigiano Reggiano

Instructions:

Preheat the oven to convection 450°F. Cut the mushrooms and place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Season with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown and crispy.

Slice the onion and add to a pan with olive oil. Season with salt and cook on medium-low heat until caramelized. About 10 minutes. 

In the meantime, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add the pasta and cook according to package directions.

Add the white wine to the caramelized onions and let it reduce for 5 minutes. Then add the heavy cream. Stir to combine.

Add the roasted mushrooms to the sauce, followed by the truffle paste. Mix well.

Drain the pasta, reserving some pasta water. Add the pasta to the mushroom sauce and stir to combine, adding small amounts of pasta water if needed to make it creamyyyy. 

Plate and add parmigiano reggiano flakes and a drizzle of truffle oil if you have it 😍😍😍 Enjoy!

Marinade
8 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
3 garlic cloves, finely minced
3 tbsp aji amarillo paste
⅓ cup soy sauce
Juice of 1 lime
Zest of 1 lime
1 tbsp ground cumin
1 tbsp paprika
1 tbsp oregano

Combine all marinade ingredients, coat the chicken, and marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight. Grill over medium heat until the chicken is beautifully charred and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F.

2 jalapeños, seeds removed
3 garlic cloves

½ cup mayonnaise (or sour cream)
⅓ cup crumbled queso fresco or cotija cheese
1 bunch cilantro
1 tbsp aji amarillo paste
2 green onions
2 tbsp olive oil

Blend until smooth and creamy. Serve alongside the grilled chicken.

caption:
Raviolo al Uovo is one of those dishes that brings us back to our roots, with rich, golden yolks at the heart of it all (literally)! @conestoga_eggs have naturally golden yolks as their hens are fed a diet that includes marigold extract, which is a natural source of lutein, adding richness to both the pasta and that perfect runny center. 

Cooking together has allowed us to preserve traditions, create memories, and pass down what matters most. Using Nonna’s 60-year-old pasta machine makes the process even more meaningful, connecting us to a time when food was made by hand and shared with love 💕 

Ingredients: 

- 13 egg yolks and 1 whole egg @conestoga_eggs (for the dough) + 1 egg yolk per raviolo (filling) 

- 2 ½ cups 00 flour 

- 2 cups ricotta 

- ½ cup Parmigiano Reggiano 

- 1 tsp nutmeg 

- Salt, to taste 

- ½ cup butter 

- Fresh sage (optional) 

1. Make a well with the flour, add egg yolks, and mix with a fork. Knead until combined, rest for 10 minutes, then knead again until smooth. Let rest for 30 minutes. 

2. Mix ricotta, Parmigiano Reggiano, nutmeg, and salt until smooth. Transfer to a piping bag and refrigerate. 

3. Roll out the dough using a pasta machine to the second-to-last setting. 

4. Pipe ricotta in a circle to create a well for the egg yolk. 

5. Cover with another pasta sheet, press to seal, and cut with a round cutter. 

6. Cook in gently boiling salted water for 2 minutes until tender with a runny yolk. 

7. In a cold pan, melt butter on low heat, adding water gradually while stirring until emulsified. Add sage if desired. 

8. Plate, drizzle with butter, and serve immediately.

Bring a big pot of water to a boil with salt and a few bay leaves. Sometimes I add whole peppercorns if I have them on hand. 

When it comes to a boil, holding the head of the octopus dip the tentacles in and out of the water a few times. Then submerge the whole thing. 

It can take as little as 30 min or up to 1 hour depending on the size of the octopus, but general rule I’ve learnt is if you scratch the octopus the purple skin should come off easily. 

This one was roughly 1 kg and it was tender in 40 minutes. 

At this point you can throw it on the grill or chop it up for salads or other dishes.

2 cups of cherry tomatoes, cut in half 
1 cup of Kalamata olives

These 1 BOWL (or blender) fluffy, moist, and delicious cottage cheese pancakes are gluten free and refined sugar free, topped with the juiciest wild berry compote!! You can use all purpose flour for this recipe (1:1 ratio) 

4 eggs
1 1/4 cup cottage cheese
Vanilla extract to taste 
3 tablespoons maple syrup 
3/4 cup flour (GF or AP) 
3 tsp psyllium husk (if using gluten free flour) 
2 tsp baking powder 
Pinch of salt 
Compote - 2 cups berries • 2 tbsp monk fruit or maple syrup or honey (adjust to taste) • 1/2 cup water 

Blend or whisk the eggs, cottage cheese, vanilla and maple syrup until smooth. Add flour, psyllium husk, baking powder, and salt. Mix until combined. 

Heat your skillet over medium heat and add butter to coat. Pour roughly 1/3 cup of batter onto skillet, cook until bubbles appear on the surface. Flip and cook until browned. 

Add berries, sweetener of choice, and water to small saucepan over medium heat. Bring mixture to a boil. Press berries slightly to release juices. Once thickened, remove from heat and top your pancakes.

caption:
Pan de Cristal, similar to ciabatta, has a higher hydration of 100% which yields light airy loaves perfect for sandwiches! 

700g bread flour 
700g water 
2 tsp instant yeast 
15g salt 

Allow yeast to dissolve in water. 
Combine flour and salt, add the water + yeast mixture. 
The dough will be wet at this stage. 
Transfer to a dish or bowl coated in olive oil that will allow you to easily perform the “coil folds”. 
Rest for 30 minutes covered with a towel. 
After 30 minutes, lift the corners of the dough and bring to center. This will start the process of developing strength. You’ll notice it will become easier to handle as you perform the folds. 
Let rest 30 minutes. 
First coil fold: 
Reach under the dough, lift, and fold on itself. Repeat 2-4 times. 
Rest 30 minutes. Repeat this cycle 3 more times. 

Turn dough on heavily floured surface to avoid sticking. Flour the top of the dough as well. With a bench scraper, cut the dough into desired amount of loaves. Transfer to parchment lined baking sheet and let rest for 2 hours or until big air pockets/bubbles are visible on the surface. 

Preheat oven to 500°F 
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden brown and crispy. 
Trick to a perfectly cooked crumb: knock on the bottom of the bread. If it sounds like a hollow wall, it’s ready!

Dry:

Pinch of salt 

Wet:
2 eggs

1/4 cup melted butter or oil 
Vanilla extract measured with your heart 
Optional: blueberries, chocolate chips, etc.

85% hydration focaccia: 
600g bread flour or AP 
15g salt 
510g warm water 
10g instant yeast 

Combine flour and salt in a large bowl. Mix water and yeast until dissolved and add to flour mixture. Mix until just combined. No kneading required.
Let rest 30 min and perform first set up folds. Repeat again after 1 hour. 
Transfer onto oiled baking tray (I add semolina after the oil which gives it great crisp and texture) and let it rest for 20 more minutes. Stretch and dimple the dough. Add desired toppings. Bake at 450°F until golden - about 30 min.

caption:
I've been making this salad for over 5 years, and today I'm sharing my favorite version with you! It's a delicious Brussels sprout and radicchio salad with sweet and salty crushed almonds and pancetta, all tossed in a Dijon vinaigrette.
You know me, I never measure ingredients🫢 so, measure with your heart and adjust to taste. 
Ingredients:
- Brussels sprouts 
- Radicchio 
- Romaine 
- Pancetta 
- Crushed toasted almonds
- Olive oil
- Dijon mustard
- Balsamic vinegar
- Honey
- Salt (just a pinch. Pancetta is salty)

Instructions:
1. Separate the Brussels sprout leaves, keeping them whole for added texture. Cut off the tips to release the leaves.
2. Thinly slice the radicchio and romaine into strips.
3. In a bowl, combine the Brussels sprouts and radicchio, and toss with the dressing. Let it sit to allow the Brussels sprouts to become more tender.
4. Cut the pancetta into small pieces and brown them in a pan until crispy. Transfer to a cutting board and finely chop.
5. Crush or roughly chop the toasted almonds. 
6. Mix the almonds with the pancetta.
7. Plate the Brussels sprouts and radicchio mixture, then sprinkle the crunchy topping over it.
8. Enjoy!

caption:
Homemade hummus >>> 
Topped with crispy sumac chickpeas and parsley

I have been making a lot of hummus lately! I have adjusted my technique which has made a huge difference in the final product. It doesn’t last long in this house! 

Here are some tips:

1. Peel the chickpeas. 
- Tedious, time consuming, but so worth it when it comes to the final texture. No more grainy hummus!! 
2. Ice cold water or an ice cube when blending. 
- Makes it fluffier and creamier! I have tried both and I find they work the same. 
3. Good quality ingredients. 
- Always! Tahini, extra virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, fresh garlic, etc. 
4. Fully cooked (or even over-cooked) chickpeas are a must. 
- For convenience, I usually use a good brand of canned cooked chickpeas. Most of the time they are soft enough, but some brands are oddly hard and crumbly. You may need to give them a quick boil to soften them up. They should “mush” effortlessly. 
5. Let it blend for at least 5 minutes. 
- I read that the best hummus is blended for 15 minutes and I can understand why! 

I encourage you to play around with ingredients/measurements, and find a texture and taste that YOU enjoy 😊

caption:
Pasta e Piselli 
This dish reminds me of my childhood 💚
It is so delicious and easy! 

4-6 people 
- 
Olive oil • 1 small white onion, diced • 1 clove of garlic, whole • 2 cups of frozen peas • 500g small pasta of choice • 2 eggs • About 1 cup grated parmigiano reggiano or pecorino (or mix of both)• salt and pepper to taste • 
*save pasta water 
Optional: red pepper flakes (add when sautéing the onions) 

Bring water to a boil and salt heavily. 
Combine eggs and grated cheese in a small bowl. Set aside. 
Add oil to hot pan. Sauté onions + garlic until translucent. Sprinkle with salt. 
Add peas and cook until tender -  about 10 minutes. 
Cook pasta in salted boiling water. 
Ladle pasta water into peas, let simmer, then blend half of the peas + more pasta water until smooth. You can discard the garlic now or blend it. 
Add pasta (al dente) into the pan, pour the blended peas and stir. Add more pasta water if needed. Pour the egg mixture and stir vigorously. It should be super creamy and rich 💚 enjoy!

Here are 5 reasons you should dry out your tomatoes too! 🍅 

1. Enjoy that summer sweetness all year long ☀️
2. Level up any dish - Drying them concentrates the flavour, making them taste even better! 
3. It’s unbelievably easy. Just prep and put in 250°F oven for 3 hours or until dried (depends on size) 
4. They store well. Submerged in oil for 1 month in the fridge or in the freezer (airtight bag or container) for 6 months to 1 year! Just in time for next years harvest! 🍅🌿
